# AIST / NMIJ — National Metrology Institute of Japan

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Country** | Japan |
| **City** | Tsukuba |
| **Tier** | Core (Tier I) |
| **Primary ecosystem** | Thermophysical databases · national metrology |
| **Signature infrastructure** | **TPDS — Network Database System for Thermophysical Property Data** |
| **R&D focus** | Nearly ideal blackbody materials · high-emissivity reference devices for thermography |

## Why it matters internationally

AIST/NMIJ is especially important as a **long-term data infrastructure**.
Its Network Database System for Thermophysical Property Data explicitly
includes both **spectral emissivity** and **hemispherical total emissivity**
among curated properties, alongside **reflectivity**; individual materials
pages show these quantities present in the archive. In parallel, AIST
reports active R&D on **nearly ideal blackbody materials** and
**high-emissivity reference devices for thermography**, placing it firmly
in the emissivity / infrared-radiometry domain rather than only in generic
materials databases. It is a crucial component of the field's **memory and
data continuity**.

## Scope of activity

### Relevant units

- **TPDS — Network Database System for Thermophysical Property Data** —
  AIST-run public resource. Database statistics explicitly list spectral
  emissivity, hemispherical total emissivity, and reflectivity among
  curated properties.
- Broader AIST / NMIJ programs on blackbody standards and thermography
  reference materials.

### Radiative properties measured / curated

Spectral emissivity · hemispherical total emissivity · reflectivity · other
thermophysical properties (broad coverage).

### Capability envelope

- **Methodology:** database infrastructure for curated thermophysical-
  property data; R&D on nearly ideal blackbody materials and high-
  emissivity reference devices for thermography.
- **Role:** provides traceability and reference-material support for the
  thermography / radiation-thermometry community in Japan and
  internationally.

### Signature infrastructure

- **TPDS (Network Database System for Thermophysical Property Data).**
  A public resource whose explicit inclusion of emissivity quantities
  makes it a genuine radiative-property database, not merely a general
  thermophysical-property archive.

### Application domains

- Thermography and radiation thermometry references
- Data curation for thermophysical properties
- Long-term accessibility and reuse of radiative-property data
- Supply of reference blackbodies and high-emissivity devices

## Why AIST / NMIJ is a reference pole

A research field only matures when it produces data infrastructures that
outlive individual projects. TPDS is one of the very few public-sector
thermophysical databases in the world that explicitly curates emissivity
quantities, and it is operated by a national metrology institute that also
produces the reference materials underpinning those measurements. That
combination — long-term database plus active reference-material R&D — is
rare, and places AIST/NMIJ in the foundational tier alongside PTB and
NIST.
